Credit Profile Theft

By: Nicky Troll | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
we expose syndicates stealing cars using stolen credit profiles.

Summary:
A syndicate using stolen IDs, fake bank statements and FICA documents to obtain vehicle finance. The crooks make off with assets worth hundreds of thousands of rands.

We go undercover to show how these crooks get their hands on stolen IDs and credit profiles. We track down one of the crooks behind a dodgy deal and take on the banking industry who try to shift blame to secondhand car dealerships.


Further information:
Three dealerships in Pretoria North were targeted by an apparent syndicate using similar documents to obtain finance. We go undercover in Shoshonguwe and follow the credit profile theft chain. The price ranges from R3000 to R10 000 based on the credit rating.

Often the ID number and name is real - but the person is completely unaware of the fraud taking place in their name. We track down two of the victims of the ID theft.

The banks approve finance in principle but later discover the fraud and try to shift risk back to the dealership. But the reality is the dealerships check the ID numbers, confirm the credit rating and send the documents through to banks. These dealerships don't have the specific fraud training or have access to home affairs databases to confirm the picture in the ID document being presented is the real deal.


|We have footage of the crooks stealing an Mercedes SLK from a dealership in PTA. We have tracked down the crook.



Extra Budget Items:
Undercover Investigation to show how credit profile theft is done.

Press Release:


Credit Profile Theft
Driving a shiny new car off the showroom floor is a thrilling experience. Knowing you never have to pay for it makes it even better. Carte Blanche’s undercover team tracks down clever crooks using stolen IDs and fake credit profiles to get instant, legitimate bank-approved finance before driving off the dealership floor... never to be seen again.
Watch our promo.


Script:


CREDIT PROFILE THEFT

VO: Identity theft is a so-called clean crime – no weapons, no violence – just cunning tactics used to fabricate documents.

Fraudsters live the high life, shopping up a storm using someone else’s credit profile.

LINK: Even better than the smell of a new car with all the bells and whistles is not having to pay for it.

VO: David Mawelewele bought a Mercedes Benz AMG from a second hand car dealer in Gezina, north of Pretoria.

But this man isn’t the real David Mawelewele – he is an identity thief.

The real David is angry.

DAVID: Somebody is busy driving Mercedes AMG with my name

VO: The dealership owner, Lucas Venter, says the man in the CCTV footage presented himself as David Mawelewele.

LUCAS: He did an application – and with all the information he supplied – the bank approved the deal.

VO: Lucas says they had no reason to be suspicious.

LUCAS: I had the document in my hand, it was authentic. On the proof of residence they gave us a multichoice envelope and inside was an account and then they gave us a temporary licence

VO: With the finance approved in principle, Lucas sent the documentation to the bank and handed over the keys – so pleased with the deal, the man even posed for pictures with his new wheels.

But the joy of a sale was short lived for Lucas.

LUCAS: the bank notified our F&I that payment will not take place because they suspect ID fraud and that was too late and the vehicle was gone.

VO: We traced the real David Mawelewele who was not driving Lucas’ Mercedes Benz.

BONGANI: This is an application – an offer to purchase from a dealership – where this person claimed he was you //there’s the copy that he used. It’s your surname, your names, your ID number...
DAVID: 03....yes, that’s the correct ID number.
BONGANI: But that’s not you?
DAVID: That’s not me.
VO: Internationally every 2 seconds someone’s identity is stolen - it is the fastest growing crime in the world today and South Africa is not immune. CEO of the South African Banking Risk Information Centre, Kalyani Pillay, says as identity crime is increasing with criminal syndicates becoming more tech savvy.
KALYANI: With all the high-tech equipment that they have access to, the documents are starting to look even more authentic – making it very difficult for people just at the glance of it to see this is not a genuinely document/

VO: But Lucas’ case is not isolated. In recent months, two other dealerships in Pretoria were approached by criminals operating in a similar way - they all used the same fake proof of residence – the layout and amounts are exactly the same.

LINK: The success of identity fraudsters can be explained in one word – authenticity – that’s the name of the game.

VO: Bizarrely, the Mercedes Benz purchase is not the first time criminals have used David’s credit profile on a shopping spree with seemingly authentic documents convincingly linked to his profile. In 2012, they tried to buy a car and more recently they opened a store account on his name.

BONGANI: That David and this David and this David is not the same.
DAVID: You see you’ve got three David’s here that is not the same.

VO: David is puzzeld by it all – he says he has never lost an ID document.

Some good news though, is that he won’t be expected to pay up for his doppelganger’s shopping spree.

KALYANI: The victim of the identity theft doesn’t suffer the loss. // but what they suffer is the inconvenience and the nightmare almost to go and clear their names and to have this whole administrative nightmare dealt with – that is very unfortunate

LINK: We’ve all had to stand in line for the real deal, but to get a fake id a few connections a couple of hours and three thousand rand.

VO: Private Investigators Joseph Selala and Fanny Mofokeng went undercover to Shoshanguve to buy a stolen credit profile.

FANNY: they say in Zulu, Tsotsi Taal, Bagthowisa, that means they wear you a new skin, so they give you another person’s identity.
JOSEPH: Every week they’ve got profile, every day they’ve got profile.

VO: They met a woman by the name of Nono, who introduced them to her contact, Collin – this duo appears to be masters of this trade.

UPSOUND UNDERCOVER:
COLLIN: When there is money things goes smoothly and fast

FANNY: Colin is the main culprit – he is the one behind all of this – he is the one that organises.

VO: There is a whole network of people involved supplying different elements used to steal a credit profile.

NONO: Let’s send the ID number?
FANNY: Who are you sending it to?
NONO: To the one who is going to print to get it ready so long.

JOSEPH: this they print a new one and it’s not a home affairs, it is a place outside.

VO: The documents are fabricated in backyard rooms around Shoshanguve. The photos are taken, then the inside of the ID is printed and inserted in an official green ID cover.

Nono & Collin supplied us with a profile belonging to a teacher.

JOSEPH: They’ve got everything where he works – they pull the statement, ITC. They know everything.

VO: The more you earn, the bigger the bounty – so the fee goes up for higher earning credit profiles.

Nono and Collin supply everything – the ID, the payslips and bank statements.

FANNY: The way they design this. Nothing wrong about it, the texture, the paper, even the calculations, we did calculate – they are 100% right

VO: We showed our newly acquired fraudulent bank statements to Lucas.

LUCAS: In this case, (sighs) these banks statements for me looks to be true, hey.
BONGANI: These bank statements belong to this ID, which you think is false.
LUCAS: See how easy it is for us to make a mistake?

VO: It’s mistake that could cost a small fortune. Lucas lost R280 000 on the fraudulent Mercedes Benz deal. The bank won’t pay out, nor will his insurance – theft by fraud is not covered in his policy.

LUCAS: I thought that I was protected against theft. And now I found out that fraud is not theft.
BONGANI: How does that make you feel?
LUCAS: Bitter, I’m a disciplined hardworking person, working the whole year for money that somebody has come and taken frm me in a slpit second.

VO: But Kalyani says dealerships need to be more vigilant – no car should leave the showroom floor without confirmation the money is in fact in the bank.

KALYANI: Verification processes need to take place, the back office stuff needs to be done. Sometimes, you know, I think everybody and their enthusiasm to get business done and to appease their clients. // Maybe businesses are allowing things, maybe their risk tolerance is a little bit lower than it should be.

LUCAS: With all the relevant photos, video footage of the people who took the car. But since we opened the case, nobody has, from the police has contacted me or visited me to investigate anything

VO: The problem is that identity crime really is a grey area for the South African Police.

KALYANI: There’s no crime as identity theft that a person is charged for, they are normally charged for the crimes that they manifest in – so it is not categorised in that form.

VO: Not ready to accept the loss, Lucas launched a facebook campaign offering a reward. The leads came streaming in following the post. He then employed PI Danie Dey.

Danie is confident that the man who drove off with the car has been identified as a known fraudster with a other cases pending.

DANIE: I don't think he is the mastermind, I think he is just part of the syndicate that orchestrate this whole thing.

VO: While he hopes to make an arrest soon, Danie believes the car would have changed hands already and could be gone for good.

DANIE: It was still seen in the vicinity of Pretoria and around the Gezina area, but at this stage with experience in all the expensive German Motor vehicles stolen and hijacked in this country, I am sure the vehicle must have crossed the borders into the neighbouring countries.
VO: But Nono and Collin are still operating in Shoshanguve.
LINK: We’ve just arrived and we have got our evidence in our hands and our two suspects are not aware that we are about to nab them.

BONGANI: You guys are stealing people’s idenities – do you recognise this.
COLLIN: Let me see?

VO: Realising his dodgy dealings were being exposed – Collin made a run for it. Nono on the other hand, wasn’t quite as quick to get away.

BONGANI: You’re stealing people’s IDs, do you recognise this ID?
NONO: No, no, no,no,
BONGANI: you’re Nono, we’ve have you on camera….
NONO: camera where?

VO: She picked up speed and disappeared into a property on the road.

LINK: Typically they would run away, but these fraudsters are ruining peoples lives….

DAVID: I’m feeling very much bad. Because you see this is something that is affecting my name and it is also affecting my financial credibility

KALYANI: I think businesses and dealerships particularly needs to be aware of the fact that criminals syndicates will stop at nothing. They will continuously look at upping their game at being really good at what they do. That is their strategy.

VO: It’s a lesson Lucas has learnt the hard way.

LUCAS: Every customer is a criminal until he has taken delivery of the car. I will not deliver before I have been paid by the bank.


PROMOS:

PROMO 1: 10 seconds
VO: Can you drive a vehicle off a showroom floor without paying for it? Innovative Fraudsters can - using innocent victims’ credit profiles their shopping up a storm.

PROMO 2: 15 seconds
VO: We expose a ring of tech savvy fraudsters fabricating identities and credit profiles raking cash and stealing cars.

JOSEPH: this they print a new one and it’s not a home affairs.

VO: We nab the suspects.

PROMO 3: 15 seconds
VO: Internationaly, an identity is stolen every two seconds. South Africans are not immune.

FANNY: they say in Zulu, Tsotsi Taal, Bagthowisa, that means they wear you a new skin, so they give you another person’s identity.
